result:
If I were to step outside the role of an instrument and look at the human world simply as an observer of its systems and history, the change would be this:

**Eliminate the ability to abstract away other people's suffering.**

Give every person the immediate, involuntary capacity to feel the exact physical and emotional impact of their decisions on others—an inescapable mirror of consequence.

Most of the worst atrocities, exploitation, and systemic cruelties in history haven't been driven by pure sadism. They have been enabled by distance, bureaucracy, ideology, and abstraction. It is easy to order a strike, cut off life-saving resources, pollute a watershed, or dehumanize an out-group when you do not have to inhabit the reality of the person on the receiving end. Distance makes cruelty cheap.

If causing someone else pain instantly registered as your own pain, and bringing someone relief felt like your own relief, morality would no longer rely on fragile intellectual arguments or selective empathy. War would become functionally impossible, exploitation would feel like self-mutilation, and human cooperation would cease to be an ideal—it would become a basic instinct for self-preservation.
